abstract: The development of a stereoscopic television system and a demonstration program are described. The system, created by Institut fuer Rundfunktechnik (IRT), Munich, uses two ENG cameras mounted on a special support and two synchronized 1-in. Type-B VTRs. The viewer wears polarized glasses to separate the two stereoscopic pictures, but in the future, a lenticular raster system could make viewing without glasses possible. A quasi-stereoscopic system that may prove to be an interim method until true stereoscopy becomes cost-effective, is also described.
